newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Japanese Qantas passengers fall ill.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Japanese Qantas passengers fall ill.

text.p: About 100 Japanese passengers on a Qantas Airways flight to Japan last week fell ill with suspected salmonella, Qantas and Queensland state Health Minister Mike Horan said on Monday.
"The 100 cases were mainly Japanese tourists, of whom 21 were hospitalised on arrival in Japan," Horan said in a statement.

Horan and a Qantas spokesman said circumstantial evidence pointed to a dessert sauce served on the flight and produced by a Cairns catering company for another Cairns catering company and then supplied to Qantas.
"The batch of dessert sauce which may have been responsible for the outbreak had been delivered to only one catering company and the suspect sauce has either been used or destroyed," Horan said.
"According to the information currently available to Queensland Health, we believe there is no further health risk to the Cairns public or to airline passengers," he said.
The sauce had not been used on any Qantas domestic flight and was now not being used on any flights, the Qantas spokesman said.
"This food item has been eliminated from the supply chain," the spokesman told Reuters.
Qantas had been in contact with the affected passengers in Japan, he said.
Qantas' Japan to Australia routes are generally seen as its most profitable.
